out.rationale: The authors take the complexity analogy that Irving et al. introduced for debate (polynomial-time judge, alternating moves) and re-apply it to their own recursive reward modeling scheme, mapping recursion depth to quantifier alternations. That is building on the cited framework with a stated change, so EXTENDS; no theorem is proved here.

text: The authors map reward modeling to NP (an agent proposes, a user verifies in polynomial time) and recursion depth to alternating quantifiers, crediting the analogy to complexity theory to Irving et al. (2018). They draw from it that evaluation is plausibly easier than production and that recursive reward modeling could cover a very general space of tasks.
title: Leike et al. apply Irving et al.'s complexity-theory analogy to recursive reward modeling
